newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures close lower, cold damage seen minor.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures close lower, cold damage seen minor.

text.p: FCOJ futures retraced recent gains and settled sharply weaker, pressured by talk that freeze damage to Florida citrus would be minimal, market sources said.
The Florida Citrus Commission said late Wednesday that state Department of Agriculture inspectors found only small pockets of damage to fruit.
Overall, the cold temperatures are not expected to slash output of the 1996/97 crop, estimated at a record 220 million 90-lb boxes.
One Florida-based analyst warned that it is still too soon to gauge losses, and added that an official report has not been released.
Today's losses were blamed on speculative selling, which broke through stops and pressured the March contract to the day's low of of 82.25.
The contract ended at 83.90 cents, down 2.95, traded 87.55 to 82.25 cents. The back months settled 2.70 to 2.40 cents weaker.
Analysts are looking for prices to continue on a downward path, and pegged support below the market at 81.30. Longer term support was seen at 76.40 cents.
